newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik opposition says not involved in border clash.
newsitem.headline: Tajik opposition says not involved in border clash.

text.p: Tajikistan's opposition leader on Wednesday denied any involvement of his forces in a clash on the border between the former Soviet republic and Afghanistan.

Russian borderguards, who patrol the border under an agreement with the Tajik government, have said about 30 opposition guerrillas were killed on Tuesday as they attempted to cross into Tajikistan east of the capital Dushanbe.
"Our fighters were not trying to cross the border," Akbar Turajonzoda, hardline deputy leader of the United Tajik Opposition, told Reuters by telephone from the Iranian capital Tehran.
"We have confirmation there was heavy shelling (by Russian forces) of Afghan territory close to where our fighters are based," Turajonzoda said, "But we suffered no casualties."

The commander of the opposition's armed forces, Davlat Usmon, said in Dushanbe that his forces were not involved in the clash, pointing instead to unnamed Afghan armed gangs. He gave no further details.
The reported clash came as the Islamic opposition and the republic's secular government prepared to sign a peace agreement on June 27 to end a four-year civil war.
A ceasefire, brokered by the United Nations, Russia and Iran last December, has largely held. The two sides have agreed a power-sharing deal but some outstanding issues remain.
"We consider this incident a provocation by some circles of the Russian military," Turajonzoda said.

The conflict has killed tens of thousands and displaced many more among the republic's 5.7 million population. Russia has some 20,000 troops in Tajikistan carrying out peace-keeping duties and guarding its frontiers with Afghanistan and China.
Tajik opposition fighters have operated out of camps inside northern Afghanistan. The remote, mountainous border also plays host to drug traffickers.
